Meet your dentists

Many dental problems need more than one kind of expertise. At Smile Zone, two specialists work under one roof, so you are not sent from one clinic to another for different parts of your treatment.

Dr. Aashay Shah

BDS, MDSPeriodontistImplantologist

A periodontist looks after the gums and the bone that hold your teeth in place. Dr. Aashay treats bleeding and swollen gums, loose teeth and receding gums, and does deep cleaning, gum surgery and dental implants. If you have lost a tooth, he will check whether your bone and gums can support an implant and plan your treatment from there.

Dr. Disha Shah

BDS, MDSEndodontist

An endodontist works on the inside of the tooth, the nerve and the root canals. Dr. Disha does root canal treatment, re-treatment of old root canals that have started hurting again, and care for cracked or badly decayed teeth. Her aim is simple: save your natural tooth wherever it can be saved.

Check-ups and everyday care

The basics that keep small problems from turning into big ones.

Digital dental X-ray

A digital X-ray shows what the eye cannot: decay between teeth, infection at the root tip, bone levels and hidden wisdom teeth. The image appears on screen within seconds, so we can show you exactly what we see. Digital X-rays also use much less radiation than old film X-rays.

Helps with: hidden cavities, root infection, implant and root canal planning

Tooth coloured composite filling

Composite fillings are matched to the shade of your teeth, so no one can tell the tooth was ever filled. The material bonds to the tooth, which means less healthy tooth is drilled away than with old silver fillings.

Helps with: cavities, chipped edges, replacing old dark fillings

Teeth cleaning, polishing and bleaching

Scaling removes hard tartar that brushing cannot, polishing lifts tea, coffee and tobacco stains, and bleaching lightens the natural shade of your teeth. A cleaning every six months keeps gums healthy and breath fresh.

Helps with: yellow or stained teeth, tartar, bad breath

Teeth removal

Some teeth cannot be saved because of deep decay, a fracture, advanced gum disease, or a wisdom tooth that is stuck or pressing on its neighbour. Extraction is done under local anaesthesia, and you go home with clear aftercare instructions and a plan for the gap.

Helps with: painful wisdom teeth, broken or badly decayed teeth

Saving and replacing teeth

Keep your natural teeth where possible, and replace missing ones with options that look and feel right.

Root canal treatment

When decay or a crack reaches the nerve, the tooth hurts with hot, cold or chewing. Dr. Disha, our endodontist, removes the infected pulp, cleans and seals the canals, and saves the tooth. It is done under local anaesthesia and usually finished with a cap.

Helps with: toothache, lingering sensitivity, swelling, a darkened tooth

Metal, zirconia and ceramic caps

A cap, or crown, covers a weak or root canal treated tooth to protect it and restore its shape. Metal caps are strong and budget friendly, ceramic caps match your tooth colour, and zirconia caps give a natural look with high strength. We help you pick based on where the tooth is and how hard it works when you chew.

Helps with: teeth after root canal, cracked or heavily filled teeth, bridges

Dental implants

A fixed replacement for a missing tooth that looks and works like your own. Dr. Aashay, our implantologist, places the implant in the jawbone and fixes a crown on top, so the teeth on either side are not trimmed the way they are for a bridge.

Helps with: a missing tooth, loose dentures, a tooth that cannot be saved

Flexible partial and complete dentures

Flexible partial dentures use a soft, gum coloured material that grips your remaining teeth comfortably, with no visible metal hooks. Complete dentures replace a full set of teeth and are shaped to your mouth, so you can chew, speak and smile with confidence.

Helps with: several missing teeth, all teeth missing, old loose dentures

Gums, kids and your smile

Specialist gum care, straighter teeth, and a smile you are happy to show.

Treatment of pyorrhoea (gum disease)

Pyorrhoea, or periodontitis, is an infection of the gums and bone that hold your teeth. Dr. Aashay, our periodontist, treats it with deep cleaning, root planing and gum surgery where needed, so you can keep your natural teeth for longer.

Helps with: bleeding gums, pus, receding gums, loose teeth

Orthodontic braces treatment

Braces gently move crowded, gapped or forward teeth into line and correct a bite that does not close properly. Straight teeth are easier to keep clean, and braces work for adults as well as children when the gums are healthy.

Helps with: crowded teeth, gaps, forward teeth, bite problems

Paediatric dentistry

Dental care for children, from the first milk tooth to the teenage years. We keep visits calm and friendly, treat decay in milk teeth early, and teach good brushing habits so your child grows up without a fear of the dentist.

Helps with: cavities in milk teeth, toothache in kids, a first check-up

Dental veneers and smile designing

Veneers are thin, tooth coloured shells fixed on the front of your teeth to cover stains, chips, gaps and uneven shapes. Smile designing plans the shape, size and shade of your teeth together so the result suits your face. A popular choice before weddings and big occasions.

Helps with: stained or chipped front teeth, gaps, an uneven smile

Questions patients ask us

Is root canal treatment painful?

The area is numbed with local anaesthesia before we start, so most people feel pressure rather than pain. The toothache you came in with usually settles once the infection is cleaned out.

How many sittings does a root canal need?

Many root canals are finished in one or two sittings. A tooth with a heavy infection or curved canals can take longer. You will know your plan after the first examination.

Can I get a dental implant?

Most healthy adults with a missing tooth can get an implant, as long as there is enough bone and the gums are healthy. Diabetes and smoking can affect healing, so we check these at your consultation.

Why do my gums bleed when I brush?

Bleeding gums are usually caused by plaque and tartar along the gumline. A professional cleaning often sorts it out. If the bleeding comes with bad breath or loose teeth, get it checked soon.

Am I too old for braces?

No. Teeth can be moved at any age as long as the gums and bone supporting them are healthy.

What is pyorrhoea and can it be treated?

Pyorrhoea is the common name for periodontitis, a gum infection that slowly destroys the bone holding your teeth. Caught early, it can be controlled with deep cleaning and good home care. Advanced cases may need gum surgery. The sooner it is treated, the more teeth you keep.

Are digital dental X-rays safe?

Yes. A digital dental X-ray uses a very small dose of radiation, much lower than old film X-rays. We only take one when it is needed to diagnose or plan your treatment.

At what age should my child first visit a dentist?

Ideally when the first milk tooth appears, or by the first birthday. Early visits help catch decay in milk teeth and get your child comfortable with the dentist.
